programme.title: Mark Lawson Talks to...
programme.desc: Julian Barnes won the 2011 Man Booker Prize for `The Sense of an Ending' and his latest novel, `Levels of Life' is a memoir of bereavement following the loss of his wife to cancer. Here he talks to Mark Lawson about love, death, memory and grief.

programme.title: My Garden of a Thousand Bees
programme.desc: Wildlife film-maker Martin Dohrn is bee obsessed. He has found over 60 species in his Bristol garden, from giant bumblebees to scissor bees the size of a mosquito, which he films with mind-blowing results. Dohrn can identify individual insects and forms a remarkable relationship with one leaf-cutter bee he follows through its entire life.

programme.title: Fred Dibnah's Magnificent Monuments
programme.desc: This edition focuses on places of worship, taking in Preston, County Durham, St Paul's Cathedral and York Minster.

programme.title: Wainwright's Walks: Coast to Coast
programme.desc: Julia sets out on the final stage. Robin Hood's Bay is the goal, but first she must complete the North York Moors and walk through Eskdale, before getting a first glimpse of the North Sea. The woods of Littlebeck and the clifftop finale provide an opportunity to reflect on a great adventure.

programme.title: A Timewatch Guide
programme.desc: Using 70 years of BBC history archive film, Professor Alice Roberts uncovers how the iconic ancient monument of Stonehenge has been interpreted, argued over and debated by some of Britain's leading historians and archaeologists. She reveals how new discoveries would discredit old theories, how astronomers and geologists became involved in the story and why, even after centuries of study, there's still no definitive answer to the mystery of Stonehenge.

programme.title: A Night on the Town
programme.desc: Musical spectacular, first broadcast in 1983, showcasing the work of Irving Berlin, Noel Coward, George Gershwin and Cole Porter. programme.title: Mindful Escapes: Breathe, Release, Restore
programme.desc: Mindfulness is the ability to be present with a clear, calm, curious mind. And feelings of joy can be triggered when this happens. How can watching penguins pinching pebbles, seeing antelope leaping in the air or looking at scenes of summer flowers help us to feel more positive emotionally? Mindfulness expert Andy Puddicombe takes us on a global journey with imagery that will bring feelings of happiness and wellbeing to the viewer.

programme.title: In Our Blood: The Forever Chemicals Scandal
programme.desc: In almost every respect, Bentham is a quintessential Yorkshire town: proud, close-knit and set against breathtaking countryside. Two years ago, an environmental journalist's investigation revealed it to be the most contaminated place ever recorded in the UK for PFAS - toxic so-called forever chemicals, some of which are linked to cancers and other serious illnesses. For decades, the town's main employer, Angus Fire, produced firefighting foam now believed to be the likely source of the pollution. The company routinely manufactured and tested this foam on site; the government ultimately banned it in 2025. This groundbreaking documentary reveals how those chemicals may have spread beyond the factory boundary and how a small town is coming to terms with what it means for them.
